note: Well-documented historical event, corroborated by every reference source.
text: The World Health Organization declared the COVID-19 outbreak a pandemic on 11 March 2020. Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the agency was deeply concerned by the alarming levels of spread and severity. At the time of the announcement more than 118,000 cases had been reported in 114 countries. The WHO urged governments to scale up testing, isolation and contact tracing.

note: Apollo 11 — among the most heavily documented events in history.
text: Apollo 11 landed the first humans on the Moon on 20 July 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent about two and a quarter hours outside the lunar module collecting samples, while Michael Collins remained in orbit aboard the command module. The mission was launched by a Saturn V rocket from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Armstrong described the landing site as the Sea of Tranquility.

note: Paris Agreement — verifiable via any reference source.
text: The Paris Agreement on climate change was adopted by 196 parties at the UN Climate Change Conference in December 2015. The treaty commits signatories to limiting global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Each country sets its own nationally determined contribution and is expected to strengthen it over time. The agreement entered into force in November 2016.

note: Higgs boson discovery, Nobel Prize 2013.
text: Physicists at CERN announced the discovery of the Higgs boson on 4 July 2012. The particle was observed independently by the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider. Peter Higgs and Francois Englert were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics the following year for predicting the mechanism that gives elementary particles mass. The measured mass of the particle was close to 125 gigaelectronvolts.

note: Mainstream, uncontroversial public-health guidance.
text: The World Health Organization recommends that adults undertake at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity each week. The guidance states that regular activity reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and several cancers. The agency also advises limiting sedentary time. These recommendations were updated in 2020 and apply to adults aged 18 to 64.

note: Structural fact about the Federal Reserve.
text: The Federal Reserve sets monetary policy in the United States through its Federal Open Market Committee, which meets eight times a year. The committee adjusts the target range for the federal funds rate to pursue maximum employment and price stability. The Federal Reserve has a stated long-run inflation objective of 2 percent. Decisions are announced in a statement released at the conclusion of each meeting.

note: James Webb Space Telescope launch.
text: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched on 25 December 2021 aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana. The observatory operates near the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point, roughly 1.5 million kilometres from Earth. Its primary mirror is composed of 18 hexagonal gold-coated beryllium segments. The telescope observes primarily in the infrared, allowing it to see through dust clouds that block visible light.

note: Chandrayaan-3 — widely reported internationally.
text: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023, making India the fourth country to achieve a soft landing on the Moon. The mission was operated by the Indian Space Research Organisation. The lander was named Vikram and carried a rover called Pragyan. The landing followed the partial failure of the Chandrayaan-2 mission four years earlier.

note: Ordinary institutional reporting, no extraordinary claims.
text: The International Monetary Fund publishes its World Economic Outlook twice a year, in April and October, with updates in January and July. The report contains growth projections for member economies and analysis of global financial conditions. The organisation was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods conference. It currently has 190 member countries.

note: Uncontroversial scientific consensus statement.
text: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change concluded in its Sixth Assessment Report that human influence has unequivocally warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land. The report was produced by hundreds of scientists reviewing thousands of peer-reviewed studies. It found that global surface temperature was about 1.1 degrees Celsius higher in 2011 to 2020 than in 1850 to 1900. The working group contributions were released between 2021 and 2022.

note: Dry institutional copy — should not be penalised for being boring.
text: The United Nations General Assembly is composed of all 193 member states, each of which has one vote. Regular sessions begin in September each year and are presided over by an elected president. Decisions on important questions, such as those on peace and security or budgetary matters, require a two-thirds majority. Other questions are decided by a simple majority.

note: Established astronomy, no controversy.
text: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched into low Earth orbit in April 1990 and remains operational more than three decades later. A flaw in its primary mirror was corrected during a servicing mission in December 1993. The telescope has been serviced by astronauts five times in total. Its observations contributed to measurements of the rate of expansion of the universe.

note: Structural fact about the RBI.
text: The Reserve Bank of India is the country's central bank and was established in 1935. Its Monetary Policy Committee sets the benchmark repo rate and is required to maintain retail inflation within a tolerance band around a 4 percent target. The committee has six members and meets bi-monthly. The bank also regulates the country's commercial banking sector.

note: Uncontroversial, well-sourced institutional fact.
text: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine has been awarded annually since 1901, with a small number of interruptions during the two world wars. The prize is decided by the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute in Sweden. It may be shared by up to three laureates in a given year. The award ceremony is held in Stockholm on 10 December, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.

note: Established fact with specific figures — exercises numeric claim handling.
text: The Large Hadron Collider at CERN is the world's largest particle accelerator, with a ring 27 kilometres in circumference located on the Franco-Swiss border. It first circulated beams in September 2008. The machine collides protons at energies of up to 13.6 teraelectronvolts. It is operated by an international collaboration involving thousands of scientists.

note: Ordinary, dry economic reporting with numbers.
text: The European Central Bank sets monetary policy for the euro area, which currently comprises 20 member states. Its Governing Council aims for inflation of 2 percent over the medium term. The bank is headquartered in Frankfurt and began operating in 1998. Interest rate decisions are announced roughly every six weeks and are followed by a press conference.
